text: Aurelia is the second largest island of the Meridian Archipelago, covering 240 square kilometers.
Aurelia has a population of exactly 12,000. The census is taken every ten years.
Aurelia was founded in 1698 by Maren Voss. The founding festival is held every year.
The highest point of Aurelia is Mount Sable, at 420 meters.
Aurelia is known for its salt.
The ferry from Aurelia to Port Halcyon runs twice daily.
Aurelia celebrates its founding day on the first day of spring.
The Aurelia tide log is kept by the harbor office.
Borin is the third largest island of the Meridian Archipelago, covering 180 square kilometers. The survey was completed in 1762.
Borin has a population of exactly 8,500. The count includes the harbor wards.
Borin was founded in 1712 by Tomas Rill.
The highest point of Borin is Rill Peak, at 380 meters.
Borin is known for its timber.
The ferry from Borin to Port Halcyon runs twice daily.
Borin celebrates its founding day on the first day of spring.
The Borin tide log is kept by the harbor office. The log covers every tide since 1700.
Calyx is the fifth largest island of the Meridian Archipelago, covering 95 square kilometers. The surveyors finished in 1763.
Calyx has a population of exactly 3,200.
Calyx was founded in 1740 by Sella Quinn.
The highest point of Calyx is Quinn Tor, at 290 meters.
Calyx is known for its azure dye.
The ferry from Calyx to Port Halcyon runs twice daily.
Calyx celebrates its founding day on the first day of spring. The festival opens with the dye parade.
The Calyx tide log is kept by the harbor office. The log is bound in blue leather.
Drennor is the largest island of the Meridian Archipelago, covering 310 square kilometers.
Drennor has a population of exactly 15,600.
Drennor was founded in 1681 by Drennor Hale.
The highest point of Drennor is Hale Crag, at 510 meters.
Drennor is known for its iron.
The ferry from Drennor to Port Halcyon runs twice daily. The crossing takes three hours.
Drennor celebrates its founding day on the first day of spring. The ironworks close for the day.
The Drennor tide log is kept by the harbor office.
Esmara is the smallest island of the Meridian Archipelago, covering 60 square kilometers.
Esmara has a population of exactly 1,800.
Esmara was founded in 1766 by Petyr Ank.
The highest point of Esmara is Ank Hill, at 150 meters.
Esmara is known for its pearls. The pearl divers work the southern beds.
The ferry from Esmara to Port Halcyon runs twice daily. The crossing takes two hours.
Esmara celebrates its founding day on the first day of spring.
The Esmara tide log is kept by the harbor office.
Falwick is the fourth largest island of the Meridian Archipelago, covering 145 square kilometers.
Falwick has a population of exactly 6,400.
Falwick was founded in 1703 by Wren Falwick.
The highest point of Falwick is Falwick Rise, at 260 meters. The summit holds a signal beacon.
Falwick is known for its wool. The wool fair buys the whole clip.
The ferry from Falwick to Port Halcyon runs twice daily.
Falwick celebrates its founding day on the first day of spring.
The Falwick tide log is kept by the harbor office.
Gannel is the sixth largest island of the Meridian Archipelago, covering 88 square kilometers.
Gannel has a population of exactly 2,900.
Gannel was founded in 1755 by Ivo Gannel.
The highest point of Gannel is Gannel Bluff, at 310 meters.
Gannel is known for its copper.
The ferry from Gannel to Port Halcyon runs twice daily.
Gannel celebrates its founding day on the first day of spring.
The Gannel tide log is kept by the harbor office.
The lighthouse on Cape Sable was built in 1776 by the Meridian Trading Company. It is maintained by the harbor office.
The lighthouse on Cape Sable is 40 meters tall.
The Grand Causeway was built in 1798 by the Council of Seven. It carries the iron road north.
The Grand Causeway is 12 kilometers long.
The Hale Observatory was built in 1822 by Sable Vane. Its great lens was ground on Calyx.
The Hale Observatory is 25 meters tall.
The Fort Rennick was built in 1705 by Governor Rennick. Its guns were never fired in anger.
The Fort Rennick is 18 meters tall.
The Salt Vaults of Aurelia was built in 1720 by Maren Voss. They hold the treaty originals.
The Salt Vaults of Aurelia is 200 meters long.
The Calyx Dye Works was built in 1761 by Sella Quinn. Its vats use the azure pigment.
The Calyx Dye Works is 50 meters long.
The Gannel Copper Smelter was built in 1788 by Ivo Gannel. Its chimney is the tallest on Gannel.
The Gannel Copper Smelter is 35 meters tall.
The Borin Timber Yards was built in 1715 by Tomas Rill. They supply the Doss Drydock.
The Borin Timber Yards is 300 meters long.
The Rennick Granary was built in 1708 by Governor Rennick. It feeds the garrison through winter.
The Rennick Granary is 60 meters long.
The Voss Memorial was built in 1801 by the Council of Seven. Fresh flowers arrive every week.
The Voss Memorial is 15 meters tall.
The Gannel Tide Mill was built in 1770 by Ivo Gannel. It grinds only at the flood tide.
The Gannel Tide Mill is 22 meters tall.
The Quinn Arboretum was built in 1752 by Sella Quinn. Its oldest tree predates the charter.
The Quinn Arboretum is 90 meters long.
The Ank Pearl Market was built in 1775 by Petyr Ank. The best lots sell before noon.
The Ank Pearl Market is 70 meters long.
The Doss Drydock was built in 1795 by Captain Lira Doss. It can take ships of forty meters.
The Doss Drydock is 80 meters long.
Port Halcyon harbor was dredged to a depth of exactly 30 meters in 1810. The dredging took four years.
Port Halcyon harbor can berth forty ships at once.
The Esmara Pearl Fleet was commissioned in 1790 with twenty-four ships. Each ship carries a white sail.
The Esmara Pearl Fleet sails under a white sail.
Sable Vane wrote the Annals of the Meridian in 1830. The manuscript fills twelve volumes.
Governor Rennick ordered the Salt Vaults sealed in 1731.
Harbor Master Joss Merrin has kept the Port Halcyon tide log since 1815. The log is kept in the Salt Vaults.
Captain Lira Doss commands the Meridian Star.
Archivist Pell Norr catalogued the council records in 1840. The catalogue runs to nine hundred pages.
Maren Voss signed the Treaty of Still Water in 1785.
Wren Falwick planted the first wool flocks in 1704. The first shearing was in 1706.
Drennor Hale mapped the northern reefs in 1690.
Tomas Rill surveyed the Borin timber stands in 1710. The survey maps every stand.
Sella Quinn bred the first azure dye vats in 1758.
Petyr Ank dove the Esmara pearl beds in 1762.
Ivo Gannel assayed the Gannel copper lode in 1750.
The Treaty of Still Water was signed in 1785. The original hangs in the Salt Vaults.
The Great Gale of 1802 destroyed twelve ships. The wreck of the Meridian Star lies off Calyx.
The first Council of Seven convened on Aurelia in 1700.
The Salt Riots shook Aurelia in 1731. The ringleaders were pardoned in 1740.
The Festival of Tides has been held on Esmara every year since 1770. The pearl divers lead the procession.
The Meridian Star was launched in 1780.
The northern reef was charted in 1690. The chart is kept at the Hale Observatory.
The Council of Seven abolished the salt tax in 1745. The repeal was read on every island.
The Calyx dye monopoly was granted in 1765.
The Gannel copper strike began in 1788. The first ingots shipped in 1789.
The Borin timber compact was signed in 1720. The compact was renewed in 1780.
The Esmara pearl divers guild held its first muster in 1772.
The Falwick wool fair was founded in 1710. The fair opens on the first market day.
The Drennor iron road was completed in 1790. The road runs from the mines to the port.
No volcano has erupted in the archipelago in recorded history.
Aurelia lies 45 kilometers north of Borin.
Borin lies 60 kilometers east of Calyx.
Calyx lies 80 kilometers south of Drennor.
Drennor lies 120 kilometers west of Aurelia.
Esmara lies 35 kilometers south of Falwick.
Falwick lies 55 kilometers east of Gannel.
Gannel lies 70 kilometers north of Calyx.
Aurelia lies 110 kilometers northeast of Drennor.
Borin lies 90 kilometers southeast of Esmara.
Calyx lies 40 kilometers west of Falwick.
Drennor lies 150 kilometers northwest of Gannel.
Esmara lies 65 kilometers southwest of Borin.
Aurelia receives 800 millimeters of rain each year.
Borin receives 1100 millimeters of rain each year.
Calyx receives 1400 millimeters of rain each year.
Drennor receives 950 millimeters of rain each year.
Esmara receives 700 millimeters of rain each year.
Falwick receives 1000 millimeters of rain each year.
Gannel receives 850 millimeters of rain each year.
The prevailing wind of the archipelago blows from the west.
The azure kingfisher nests only on Calyx.
Silver fern grows on the slopes of Hale Crag.
The giant tortoises of Esmara live for over a hundred years.
Black coral fringes the reefs south of Borin.
The Drennor ironwood takes eighty years to mature.
Salt grass covers the Aurelia flats.
The Falwick moor hare turns white in winter.
Gannel cave bats navigate the smelter tunnels.
The Calyx dye snail yields azure pigment.
Pearl oysters cluster in Esmara lagoon.
The Aurelia gull follows the ferry every day.
Storm petrels nest on the cliffs of Gannel.
The salt run sails from Aurelia to Drennor.
The timber run sails from Borin to Aurelia.
The dye run sails from Calyx to Esmara.
The iron run sails from Drennor to Gannel.
The pearl run sails from Esmara to Calyx.
The wool run sails from Falwick to Borin.
The copper run sails from Gannel to Falwick.
The Meridian Star is sixty meters long.
The Meridian Star flies the seven-star flag.
No ship may enter Port Halcyon after dark.
The Council of Seven meets on Aurelia.
Each councillor serves a term of exactly seven years.
The council records are kept in the Salt Vaults.
Aurelia holds two council seats.
Drennor holds two council seats.
Borin holds one council seat.
Calyx holds one council seat.
Esmara, Falwick, and Gannel share one council seat.
In 1690, Drennor Hale charted the northern reef.
In 1700, the first Council of Seven convened.
In 1704, Wren Falwick planted the first wool flocks.
In 1710, Tomas Rill surveyed the Borin timber stands.
In 1720, the Salt Vaults of Aurelia were completed.
In 1731, the Salt Riots shook Aurelia.
In 1745, the Council of Seven abolished the salt tax.
In 1750, Ivo Gannel assayed the Gannel copper lode.
In 1758, Sella Quinn bred the first azure dye vats.
In 1762, Petyr Ank dove the Esmara pearl beds.
In 1770, the Festival of Tides was first held on Esmara.
In 1780, the Meridian Star was launched.
In 1785, the Treaty of Still Water was signed.
In 1802, the Great Gale destroyed twelve ships.
The Aurelia salters guild was chartered in 1725.
The Borin shipwrights guild was chartered in 1718.
The Calyx dyers guild was chartered in 1763.
The Drennor ironsmiths guild was chartered in 1792.
The Esmara pearl divers guild was chartered in 1772.
The Falwick weavers guild was chartered in 1712.
The Gannel coppersmiths guild was chartered in 1790.
The first salt flat on Aurelia was worked by Maren Voss in 1700.
The first timber stand on Borin was worked by Tomas Rill in 1710.
The first dye vat on Calyx was worked by Sella Quinn in 1758.
The first iron forge on Drennor was worked by Drennor Hale in 1695.
The first pearl bed on Esmara was worked by Petyr Ank in 1762.
The first wool flock on Falwick was worked by Wren Falwick in 1704.
The first copper lode on Gannel was worked by Ivo Gannel in 1750.
In 1701, the Council of Seven decreed that the ferry tolls were fixed.
In 1725, the Council of Seven decreed that the guild charters were confirmed.
In 1740, the Council of Seven decreed that the reef lights were ordered.
In 1755, the Council of Seven decreed that the dye export duty was set.
In 1778, the Council of Seven decreed that the harbor curfew was lifted.
In 1799, the Council of Seven decreed that the iron road tolls were set.
In 1812, the Council of Seven decreed that the tide logs were made public.
